sentences.text: This judgment arise out of claim petition filed by the claimant against respondents under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "Act") praying for awarding compensation of Rs.20,00,000/- for the injuries sustained in a road traffic accident that occurred on 15.11.2023 at about 12.00pm.

2. The case of the claimant in nutshell is that:
On 15.11.2023 at about 12.00pm when the petitioner was crossing the Road in front of house of D.G.P. i.e., the Director General of Police, Bengaluru at Nrupathunga Road, suddenly a rider of the Splendor Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HN-2372 came from K.R.Circle towards Corporation circle with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering human life and dashed to the petitioner.
Due to impact, the petitioner fell down and suffered grievous injuries.
Immediately, she was shifted to Martha's Hospital, Bangalore treated as an inpatient from 15.11.2023 to 18.11.2023 and discharged with advice.

So far she has spent huge amount towards her treatment,
nourishment, food etc., Due to the said accidental injuries, suffering from permanent disability.
The injuries caused in the accident are permanent in nature.
3. It is the case of the petitioner that, Prior to accident the petitioner was hale and healthy, working in the office of BBMP as Sweeper and getting salary of Rs.20,767/- per month.

The said accident occurred due to sole rash and negligent riding by the rider of the bike bearing Registration No.KA-02-HN- 2372 and Halasur Traffic Police have registered a case against the rider of the bike in Cr.No.92/2023.
The Respondent being the RC owner of the offending vehicle are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
Hence, the petitioner prayed to allow the petition and to grant compensation as prayed in the petition.

4. In response to the notice, the respondent did not appear before this court hence, place ex- parte.
5.
Basing on the pleadings of the parties, the following Points are framed for determination.

Point No.1: Whether the petitioner proves that, the accident occurred on 15.11.2023 at about 12.00pm due to rash and negligent riding by the rider of the Spendor Bike bearing Reg.No.KA-02-HN-2372 and in the said accident petitioner sustained injuries?
Point No.2: Whether the petitioner is entitled for Compensation?
If so, what is the quantum?
From whom?
Point No.3: What Order or Award?
6. In order to substantiate the claim petition contention, the petitioner has examined herself as PW-1 and got marked Seventeen documents as Exs.P1 to P17.

sentences.text: The Court has heard the arguments canvassed by learned counsel for the petitioner.
8. On perusal of oral and documentary evidence let in before this tribunal, my answers to the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 :In the affirmative, Point No.2: Partly in affirmative.

Point No.3: As per final order, for the foregoing #REASONS#
9.
Point No.1:-
In order to substantiate the claim petition, the petitioner has examined herself as PW.1 and got marked Ex.P1 to 17.
The details of the exhibits are given in the annexure of the judgment.
There is no cross examination of the petitioner.

10. The petitioner has produced the police documents, the police documents have clearly indicates that, the investigating officer after conducting thorough enquiry, recording the statements of the witnesses and after visiting the seen of occurrence has submitted the charge sheet against rider of offending Bike.
11. Among the documents produced, Ex.P-1 is the FIR, in which it is mentioned that the accident had occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of rider of offending Bike.
The police registered the case against the accused for the offence punishable under section 279, 338 of Indian Penal Code and Sec.146, 196 of MV Act.
The petitioner has produced the charge sheet.
The charge sheet clearly demonstrated that the rider of the Bike rode the vehicle without possessing the valid insurance.
Therefore, I hold that the accident is caused due to sole rash and negligent riding of the offending Bike.

12. Thus, on an overall consideration of these documents coupled with the evidence of PW-1, it would clearly establish that the accident in question had occurred due to the negligence of the rider of Bike bearing Reg. No.KA-02-HN-2372.
Therefore, I hold that the accident is caused due to sole rash and negligent rider of the offending Bike.
The Court cannot adopt strict liability as conducted in a criminal case to prove rash and negligence on the part of the rider of the respondent vehicle.
But there should be prima-facie materials regarding rash and negligence to fix the owner and insurance company for payment of compensation.
It can be gathered in the police records that the complaint has been lodged with delay.
In the light of the Judgment in 1RAVI's case, it is manifestly clear delay in lodging the FIR cannot be the ground to deny justice to the victim.
However, the claim has to be examined with a closer scrutiny, particularly the contents of the FIR.
The First Information report indicates that, the informant had not lodged the complaint as he was busy in taking care of the injured person in the hospital.
So, the informant has shown the reason for lodging the complaint with delay.
Same has been highlighted in the relevant column of FIR.
So, the reasons assigned by the informant is satisfactory and cogent reasons for it.
There could be variety of reasons in genuine cases for delayed lodgment of FIR.
In such cases, the authenticity of the FIR assumes much more significance than delay in lodging thereof.

It is well settled position of law that the proceedings under Motor Vehicle Act are summary in nature and it is beneficial legislation and the evidence required about negligence act is sufficient if it is in the nature of preponderance of probability.
Hence, I hold Point No.1 in the affirmative.

sentences.text: Point No.2: the claimant has produced Wound Certificate as per Exhibit P-8.
It shows that the claimant has sustained (1) lacerated wound present over left parietal temporal region bone deep.

(2)
Lacerated wound present over right lateral aspect of elbow bone deep. (3) Lacerated wound over right small toe bone deep.
(4) Abrasion present over right knee and (5) Fracture of the right leg proximal tibia near the right knee.
Out of these injures, injury Nos.1, 2, 3 and 4 are simple in nature and injury No.5 is grievous in nature.

Though the petitioner has produced the discharge summary,
he has failed to examine the medical officer to substantiate the permanent disability as pleaded.

So,
I am of the opinion that though the claimant is able to prove that she has sustained injuries in the road traffic accident but she has failed to prove that she had sustained permanent disability due to injuries sustained in the road traffic accident.
Considering the contents of wound certificate and nature of injury sustained in the accident, it can be presumed that claimant has taken treatment for above said injury.

The petitioner further deposed that she has spent huge amount towards treatment, conveyance, attendant charges etc., and took treatment at Martha's Hospital, Bangalore from 15.11.2023 to 18.11.2023 for total 4 days.
In this regard, petitioner has produced IP Bills at Ex.P.14 and medical bills at Ex.P15.

Therefore, by considering the nature of injuries sustained by the claimant in the road traffic accident, nature of treatment taken by her, the period in which she has taken treatment as an in- patient and also amount spent towards treatment, I am of the firm opinion that awarding a sum of Rs.3,00,000/- as global compensation under only one conventional head meets the ends of justice.
In view of, I answer Point No.2 in partly affirmative.
14. Point No.3:-
In view of my findings to the above issues, the claimant is entitled for the compensation at the at rate of 6% pa from the respondent.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER
The claim petition filed by claimant under section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 is allowed in part.

The respondent is liable to pay total compensation to the tune of Rs.3,00,000/-
(Rupees Three Lakhs only) together interest @ 6% P.A from the date of petition till realization.
The respondent is directed to deposit the said amount within 60 days from the date of this judgment after deducting any amount paid as the interim compensation.
On deposit of compensation, the petitioner is entitled to withdraw entire amount with interest as awarded amount is meager one.
The office is directed to release the entire amount to petitioner or PW.1 with interest through e-payment.
All the interim application if any pending stands disposed off.
